A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProgressCaptioner work. Their complete main texts and supplementary material, including equations, figures and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FrameCapEval experiments, a 15-participant user study, downstream video-understanding results and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a pseudo-labeling baseline and experiments with alternative automatic evaluators.

M1.justification: The architecture, two-stage pseudo-labeling pipeline, caption filtering, SFT/DPO training and inference procedures are retained. The expanded explanation of variable temporal context describes capabilities already documented in v1's supplement.

E1.justification: Both versions train on HowToChange and COIN and evaluate captioning on those datasets plus Penn Action and Kinetics. The frame-classification, keyframe/action-recognition and NExT-QA tasks are retained. The new evaluator analysis reuses HowToChange.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PL (VLM ensemble), a baseline using filtered captions from multiple VLMs. Existing captioning and downstream comparison methods remain in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The new Figure 19 introduces alternative evaluation conditions on HowToChange: GPT-4o for caption matching alongside Gemini-1.5-Pro, and GPT-4o-mini for progression detection alongside Llama-3.1. Existing splits, metrics and user-study sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplement adds an evaluator-sensitivity analysis testing whether caption-matching and progression-detection trends persist across evaluation models. The original Table 5 ablations, qualitative comparisons, keyframe analysis and failure example are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 19 compares evaluator choices without introducing statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds PL caption-matching/progression-detection scores of 18.6/62.5 on HTC, 17.6/60.1 on COIN and 19.3/52.4 on Penn&K. Figure 19 adds results under alternative evaluators. Existing benchmark, downstream, user-study and ablation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, caption-selection rules and metric definitions are retained. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same task, model, dataset and benchmark contributions, together with the caption-quality and downstream-utility claims. The new experiments support these claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: The new 'Justification of Automatic Evaluation' passage explains the reference-free evaluation choice and interprets cross-evaluator trends as evidence of robustness. Section 3.2 adds a local-versus-global temporal-context explanation. Existing limitations concerning noisy pseudo-labels, longer sequences and spatial distinctions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that video baselines receive matching temporal context and identifies user-study participants as English-fluent graduate students. However, it removes v1's explicit one-epoch SFT and DPO training statements. Supplementary hyperparameters, prompts, dataset counts and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds video paragraph captioning and cites Yu et al. (2016), 'Video paragraph captioning using hierarchical recurrent neural networks.' The broader positioning relative to image captioning, video captioning and VLMs remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and method-summary rewrites, corrects wording, reorders benchmark-description paragraphs and adds acknowledgements and a user-study heading. The overall structure remains stable. A previously valid appendix reference to Section 4.2 becomes 'Section ??'.

P2.justification: v2 adds the application illustration in Figure 2, evaluator-comparison plots in Figure 19 and the PL row in Table 1. Existing figures are resized or relocated, and Table 2 moves within the same page. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: Table 1's PL control better supports the benefit over using filtered ensemble captions directly, while Figure 19 provides targeted evidence about evaluator sensitivity on HowToChange. These additions modestly strengthen the empirical case, outweighing the loss of epoch-count documentation and the broken appendix cross-reference. The method and previously reported performance remain unchanged.
